title: The Wolf Who Learned to Control His Emotions

sentences.text: Once upon a time, there was a wolf who lived in a beautiful forest, surrounded by all his friends.
His name was Wolf.
But this wolf had a problem: he was too emotional.
Happy, angry, sad, excited... his mood changed a hundred times a minute!
So, when Wolf was in a joyful mood, he whistled with a light heart, cracked jokes, talked to the trees...
He was bursting with energy and full of fun ideas!
However, if something upset him… Oh no!
He would frown, explode, and send everyone away!
— You need to learn to calm down, Wolf, said Master Owl one day, exasperated.
You're making us dizzy!
— Learn to calm down?
But why?
asked Wolf.
— To be more peaceful!
But don’t worry, we’ll help you… We start tomorrow!
The next day, Wolf went to his friend’s house.
— To control your emotions, yoga is perfect!
declared Master Owl.
Breathe calmly and clear your mind.
Master Owl flowed through the poses: lotus, mountain… and Wolf tried to copy him.
Oh dear!
It wasn’t easy, but it was so funny!
Unable to hold it in, Wolf burst out laughing.
— Seems like yoga doesn’t work for you, sighed Master Owl.
Outside, Alfred was waiting impatiently for Wolf.
— Nothing beats sport to let off steam, he said.
I’ve set up a special “Excited Wolf” course.
Ready?
And off he shot like a rocket.

Behind him, Wolf was running, jumping, crawling…
Alfred stopped at the foot of a huge tree.
— See you at the top!
he shouted as he disappeared into the leaves.
Once at the top, Wolf looked down… His throat tightened, his heart pounded in his chest, his legs trembled.
— Alfred, I’m scared!
he panicked.
I’m going to fall!
— Calm down, Wolf.
I’m right here with you.
We’ll climb down together, slowly.
Wolf took a deep breath and, trembling all over, climbed down.
— You’ve conquered your fear—you can be proud of yourself!
Alfred congratulated him.
Wolf smiled: oh yes, he was truly proud of himself!
All this made me hungry, thought Wolf.
That’s perfect—Big Louie is waiting for me.
Covered in flour, Big Louie was in the kitchen with Lona.
— They look like they’re having so much fun together…, thought Wolf, jealous.
— Hi, Wolf!
said Big Louie.
Today we’re making macarons.
To succeed with these treats, you have to be very, very patient.
It's a great exercise for you, isn’t it?
At these words, Lona burst out laughing.
Wolf felt his temper rising.

He turned red, stomped his foot and exploded:
— That’s right, go ahead and make fun of me!
he shouted, furious.
I don’t care!
I don’t even want to make stupid cookies with stupid people!
Wolf stormed off, muttering under his breath and swiping angrily at the trees.
Little by little, Wolf slowed down, until he was dragging his feet like a snail, his heart heavy.
A tear rolled down his cheek.
— I shouldn’t have gotten angry, he sniffled.

Lona will never love me again… I feel so sad…



— Hey, what’s wrong with my awesome buddy?
came a voice behind him.
It was Miss Yeti.

She gave him a big hug, then said:
— What’s done is done.
Now you have to fix your mistake!
Go see Big Louie and Lona and apologize.
You’ll feel so much better afterward.
— But what if Lona doesn’t forgive me?
asked Wolf, worried.
— Nothing ventured, nothing gained, replied Miss Yeti.
Go on now!
Feeling ashamed, Wolf went back and knocked on Big Louie’s door.
— I’m sorry, my friends, he said.
I didn’t mean what I said.
It wasn’t kind.
— Apology accepted, smiled Lona.
Wolf and Lona looked at each other, hearts in their eyes.
Wolf lifted his paws: he felt light, light, light!
And… he was starving!
Let’s eat now —the macarons are ready!
